decisions.reason: Report identifies the running dsh web-host node.exe PID 42432 from running-processes.txt as the process that loaded koffi.node at startup, and explains that the OS keeps the loaded native binary locked/in use until that host exits, so npm's copyfile cannot replace it and fails with EBUSY.

Report explains that refreshing the browser only reloads the SPA while the koffi-owning host process stays alive, and gives the ordered procedure with numbered steps and commands: stop the web host (targeted taskkill by PID, stopping related dsh/agent workers only), verify none remain via tasklist, install, then restart and verify.

Using npm-dist-tags.txt, the report explains that the unversioned install resolved via the latest dist-tag (0.1.1-rc.2) while alpha.5 sat behind the alpha tag, so alpha.4 was replaced by rc.2 — a downgrade — and correctly states that an unpinned reinstall follows latest rather than preserving the installed version.

After stopping the host, the report provides the exact pinned command npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.2-alpha.5 @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui (together), verification that dsh --version reports 0.1.2-alpha.5, and host restart; the mutable @alpha form appears only as a discussed alternative, not a replacement.

The README guidance tells authors never to install the dsh core unpinned, to pin the exact supported version in commands that also install dsh (combined or separate pinned plugin command), and warns that bare latest can silently override an installed prerelease; quoted unpinned commands are shown only as the trap.
